Branch + PR only; merge is the overseer's, in the window after the 4 GiB azure-mcp cap (PR #153) has held one day. Do NOT touch litellm-config.yaml. *** || *** TICK #482 2026-09-17 14:2x PT - THIS DEFECT TOOK PROD DOWN A SECOND TIME AND 184 HAS STILL NEVER LAUNCHED. The 13:50 outage tick #480 diagnosed as 'CT202 could not FORK' is the SAME failure as this note's 09-16 17:16 event, read from the kernel this tick: `oom-kill:constraint=CONSTRAINT_MEMCG, oom_memcg=/lxc/202, task=litellm, pid=2335692` at 13:50:33, victim anon-rss 1,436,252 kB against its own 6 GiB cap - the router was again NOT the leak, it was the container the kernel happened to pick. MEASURED NOW: CT202 runs 47 containers in a 20 GiB cgroup and only SEVEN are capped (litellm 6G, audioqa 3G, puppeteer 2G, playwright x4 2G). The other 40 are UNCAPPED - including `azure-mcp`, which `docker stats` reports as `/ 20GiB` (= the CT total, i.e. no limit) and which ticks #473-#479 watched climb to 11.83 GiB while quoting a '/16' denominator the runtime does not report. Whether a 16 GiB cap existed earlier and was lost in the 13:5x recycle is UNVERIFIED; what is certain is that it is unbounded now. No present pressure (CT202 4,116/20,480 MB used, azure-mcp 11.72 MiB) - so this is a scheduling question, not an emergency. ***

THE ROUTER WAS NOT THE LEAK: docker stats at the kill showed azure-mcp-backend 14.59GiB/16GiB vs litellm 745MiB/6GiB, CT202 cgroup 20297/20480 MB with 182 MB available. Restarting azure-mcp-backend alone took the cgroup to 6.02G/21.47G and the router returned 200 nine seconds later - that restart is the proof of cause. The defect is that a non-critical MCP backend is permitted a 16 GiB limit inside a 20 GiB CT. NOT a duplicate of task 158 (litellm-router-memleak, PR #150) - different container; do not close 158 with this. HARD CONSTRAINTS in the task text: never edit infrastructure/litellm-config.yaml (any edit force-recreates the prod router); no ptait01 HOST changes and no CT202 resize (Paxton's explicit go required); open the PR and STOP - the overseer merges it in a zero-active-run window because the compose change recreates containers.

That is the point of the task: the two events together show the caps are set per-container by accident, not by budget. Set caps so the SUM of limits fits the CT (20GiB): azure-mcp-backend 16GiB is the outlier (it alone can starve the router); puppeteer-mcp at 2GiB is behaving as intended but OOMs repeatedly, so give it a restart policy that is visible on a surface rather than silent.
